-- FORECAST CHANGES OF NOTE/BIG PICTURE COMMENTS/PRIMARY
 UNCERTAINTIES:

- As already touched on/alluded to in the KEY MESSAGES above,
  our three biggest forecast issues/uncertainties for the 7-day
  forecast as a whole are:

1) Could some spotty/sneaky shower/thunderstorm activity "ruin"
what had been/has been a MOSTLY dry forecast between late Wed 
night-Thurs night? As of now, we have maintained a dry forecast 
for the vast majority of our forecast area (CWA), but this bears
watching just in case there is enough lift/instability to
generate at least spotty activity. Right now the NAM is the 
main primary model suggesting these chances, while the ECMWF and
especially GFS/RRFS are less supportive. 

2) How far might we be underdoing (aiming too cool) on high
temps especially Friday-Sunday? As we've clearly seen over the 
last 3-4 days, our "default" multi-model blend (NBM) has really 
been struggling to go warm enough in this recent sunnier/drier 
air weather pattern, and more "raw" deterministic model data and
"old school" numerical guidance strongly suggests that our 
official forecast is quite possibly AT LEAST 5 degrees too cool 
for Fri-Sun, as we seem primed to see more 80s vs. 70s 
(especially Fri-Sat). While we proactively adjust NBM temps 
especially in the shorter term (first few days), these periods 
are still a bit too far out in time for us to have much control 
over making adjustments, so for now this forecaster considers 
it a likely forecast weakness. 

3) Although still too far out in time (6-8 days) to even begin
thinking about providing "finer details", eventually we could 
see a return of more legitimate rain chances as a large-scale
western U.S. low pressure system/trough emerges into the 
central states. As has been seen countless times in the "model 
world" over the years, the GFS is noticeably faster with the 
arrival of rain/possible thunderstorm chances (perhaps as soon 
as Sun night-Monday), while the slower (and often more accurate)
ECMWF solution holds off rain/thunderstorm chances until more so
Tuesday-Wednesday. As is typical, our current official forecast
is a "middle ground" with rain chances arriving already Sun
night-Monday, but only "iffy" 20-30% chances. 


-- 7-DAY FORECAST CHRONOLOGICAL DETAILS (through Mon. Oct. 12, but
 heavily focused on these first 3-4 days):
- CURRENT/RECENT WEATHER SCENE AS OF 2 PM:
Although certainly on the breezy side with sustained southerly
winds commonly 12-22 MPH/gusts 16-32 MPH (lightest in our
east/strongest in our central/west), it's another virtually
cloudless/sunny day with high temps on track to top out 77-79
most places, with a mainly southwestern spots probably tagging
80 briefly. 

In the mid-upper levels, water vapor satellite/short-term model
data confirm that our Central Plains region resides under broad
west-northwesterly flow...directed between ridging over the
southwestern U.S. and a large upper low/trough over southeastern
Canada. At the surface, our breezy south winds are being driven
by a tightening pressure gradient behind a surface high pressure
axis centered over the eastern Midwest/Great Lakes (and that was
over us 24 hours ago), and a High Plains lee trough to our west. 


- THIS EVENING-OVERNIGHT:
As benign northwesterly flow aloft persists, skies remain mostly
clear and the forecast remains guaranteed dry. At the surface,
breezes slacken from this afternoon's speeds, but remain
generally southerly with sustained speeds commonly 5-15 MPH
(overall-lighest in our far west toward sunrise in our far west
toward sunrise as a weak trough axis/more westerly wind shift
arrives). Literally the only possible "forecast issue" is for a
narrow axis of least light/patchy fog to develop for a few hours
along this trough axis primarily within Dawson County in our far
west. Although this is something to keep an eye on, right now
this appears to be a very limited concern for us (both
likelihood of fog being truly dense and overall areal
coverage...affecting only a fraction of our CWA at most). Low
temps were nudged down very slightly, with mid-50s most
places...and typical cooler spots (especially
Valley/Greeley/Dawson counties) more so low 50s. 


- TUESDAY DAYTIME:

dry and no worse than mostly sunny as a whole, under continued
